radiohead>pixies.found: He could play the keyboards and then he learned the guitar very quickly, listening to Pixies and Lou Reed's New York album, and that was it.
radiohead>pixies.citation: Colin Greenwood to The Big Issue (2024), on his brother Jonny: "He could play the keyboards and then he learned the guitar very quickly, listening to Pixies and Lou Reed's New York album."
radiohead>pixies.note: Original citation (Jonny on teenage London trips to Throwing Muses and Pixies) not found; Pitchfork 2016 Monroe interview (Wikipedia fn 144) 404s. Speaker is Colin, a Radiohead member, about Jonny.

the-smiths>the-stooges.found: "At the age of 14, I was starting to play guitar in a certain way and the name [of Stooges’ guitarist] James Williamson kept cropping up," Marr told The Quietus in 2015.

the-smiths>the-stooges.note: Same Louder page also quotes Marr to Spin 2012: 'I got the first two Stooges albums immediately after I got Raw Power , and I know every note and word on them.' the-smiths>new-york-dolls.found: He was also a fan of American glam rock artists such as Sparks , Jobriath and the New York Dolls . [ 37 ] He formed a British fan club for the latter, attracting members through small adverts in the back pages of music magazines.
the-smiths>new-york-dolls.citation: Morrissey was a fan of the New York Dolls as a teenager, ran their British fan club, and wrote a 1981 booklet about them; Johnny Marr, also a Dolls fan, was impressed enough by that book to knock on his door and propose forming a band.
the-smiths>new-york-dolls.note: Wikipedia only (footnotes 37, 38 not followed). Marr's own 'girl-group guitar lineage through the Dolls' not found (one search, no hit). Tier lowered to reported.

mogwai>low.found: Low were one of the first touring bands that we got to open for and i literally could not believe how amazing they were.

On their delays: "I'm sure this inspired us to try a bit harder to use them a bit better."
